### Observed differences

- The loop around A01 was rewired. Earlier, A01 passed on almost always to A07 (about 94 in 100 of its outgoing transitions), A07 passed to A05 or A06 (about 43 and 41), and A05 passed back to A01 (about 96). In the later window, A01 passes mainly to A05 (about 57) and A06 (about 18), A05 passes to A07 (about 91), and A07 passes back to A01 (about 94). [DIR001, DIR004, DIR006]
- The immediate successions behind this changed in both directions: A01→A07, A07→A05 and A05→A01, each previously direct in about 26–29 in 100 of observed pairs, no longer occur at lag 1, while A01→A05, A05→A07, A07→A01 and A01→A06 became common direct successions (about 20–41 in 100, from zero before). [LAG003, LAG013, LAG009, LAG001, LAG011, LAG012, LAG002]
- Participation moved in opposite directions: A07 appeared in about 50 in 100 traces earlier vs about 29 in 100 later (mean occurrences per trace 1.03 → 0.57), while A01 rose from about 28 to about 53 in 100 traces (55 → 106 of 200), its mean occurrences per trace doubled (0.53 → 1.10), and it repeated within a trace in 29% of traces vs 11% before. [OCC002, OCC001]
- Within traces, A07 now sits later (mean relative position about 0.69 vs 0.51), and A06 moved from the very end of the trace (about 0.96) to the middle (about 0.48). [POS004, POS003]
- Co-occurrence followed: earlier A07 often appeared without A01 (about 23 in 100 traces); later that no longer occurs and instead A01 appears without A07 in about 24 in 100 traces. A03, A04 and A06, which earlier co-occurred with A07 in about 50 in 100 traces, now each occur without A07 in about 24 in 100 traces. [REL005, REL006, REL007, REL009]
- Upstream, A03 and A04 now pass on to A01 (about 34 and 39 in 100 of their outgoing transitions, vs about 1 and 3) and hardly to A07 (about 2 and 1 vs 51 and 41); A06 now passes to A01 and A05 rather than only to A03/A04, though its earlier profile rests on only about 11 transitions. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the cyclic sequence among A01, A05 and A07 was reordered: earlier the loop ran A01 → A07 → A05 → back to A01, while in the later window it runs A01 → A05 → A07 → back to A01 — A05 and A07 exchanged places in the cycle. Along with this, A07 is executed in fewer traces (about 50% → 29%) and later in each trace, A01 in more traces (about 28% → 53%) and more often repeated, and A06 moved from the end of the loop (after A07, passing to A03/A04) to the middle, reached from A01 and passing back into A01/A05. The reordering is shown directly by successor and immediate-succession changes that match in both directions (old direct edges vanish, new ones appear), corroborated by the relation profiles (A05 now precedes A07; A06 now precedes A07 where A07 previously preceded A06) and by the position and participation shifts; with 35 qualifying items against about 0.29 expected without change, chance sampling cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [DIR001, DIR004, DIR006, LAG001, LAG009, LAG011, LAG012, LAG013, REL003, REL008, REL009, POS003, POS004, OCC001, OCC002]

Limitations: all items come from a single control-flow family and several describe overlapping aspects of the same rewiring, so they are not independent confirmations; the evidence cannot distinguish whether A07 simply became optional in more traces or whether the loop is traversed differently, since its participation, position and edges moved together; and a few profiles rest on few observations (for example A06's earlier outgoing transitions, about 11). [REL001, REL002, REL004, DIR005, OCC001, OCC002]

Other differences: A03 and A04 now feed into A01 and A06 instead of A07, and their distances changed — A03→A01 and A04→A01 became immediate (lag-1 shares about 25 and 23 in 100, from near zero), while A03→A07 and A04→A07 moved to lags of 3–5 steps. [DIR002, DIR003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG005, LAG008]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 58 units tested, 35 items qualified, 0.29 items expected without change. That's a count many times larger than the expectation (35 vs 0.29). So the screening comparison says: this cannot be explained by chance as a whole. So we move past "Insufficient evidence" based on the count comparison.

All evidence items are control-flow family (CF_POS, CF_LAG, CF_REL, CF_DIR, CF_OCC). No time items (TWAIT), no resource items (ASSIGN/CONC/HAND). So I should not discuss time or resources.

Now let me piece together the behavioural story.

Key observations:

OCC001: A01 participation rose from 0.275 (about 55 in 200 traces) to 0.53 (about 106 in 200). Mean occurrences per trace rose from 0.525 to 1.095. Recurrence support rose from 0.11 to 0.29. So A01 became more frequent and more often repeated.

OCC002: A07 participation fell from 0.505 (about 101) to 0.29 (about 58). Mean occurrences per trace fell from 1.03 to 0.565. So A07 became less frequent.

POS003: A06 position: support 0.505 → 0.53 (similar participation), but mean position fell from ~0.96 to ~0.48. So A06 now occurs earlier in traces (position normalized presumably by trace length). Median 1.0 → 0.44.

POS004: A07 position: support 0.505 → 0.29 (participation dropped), mean position rose from ~0.51 to ~0.69. So A07 occurs later when it does occur, and less often.

POS001: A01 position: support 0.275 → 0.53, mean position roughly similar (~0.58 → ~0.61), median 0.667 both. So A01 occurs at similar position but more often.

POS002: A05 position: support 0.275 → 0.29 (similar), mean position rose from ~0.47 to ~0.57. Slight later position.

DIR001: A01's outgoing transitions: before, A01 was followed almost always by A07 (0.94 share of outgoing transitions). After, A01 is followed by A05 (0.57), A06 (0.18), A04 (0.14), A03 (0.11). So A01 no longer leads to A07; it now leads to A05 mostly.

DIR004: A05's outgoing: before, A05 followed by A01 (0.96). After, A05 followed by A07 (0.91). So A05 now leads to A07.

DIR006: A07's outgoing: before, A07 followed by A06 (0.41), A05 (0.43), A03 (0.07), A04 (0.08). After, A07 followed by A01 (0.94). So A07 now leads back to A01.

DIR005: A06's outgoing: before, A06 → A03 (0.64), A04 (0.36). After, A06 → A01 (0.31), A03 (0.28), A04 (0.14), A05 (0.18), A07 (0.08). So A06 now also leads to A01 and A05.

DIR003: A04's outgoing: before, A04 → A03 (0.40), A07 (0.41), A05 (0.08), A06 (0.08), A01 (0.03). After, A04 → A01 (0.39), A06 (0.26), A03 (0.28), A05 (0.07), A07 (0.01). So A04 now leads to A01 and A06 instead of A07.

DIR002: A03's outgoing: before, A03 → A07 (0.51), A04 (0.31), A05 (0.09), A06 (0.09), A01 (0.01). After, A03 → A04 (0.33), A01 (0.34), A06 (0.25), A05 (0.06), A07 (0.02). So A03 now leads to A01/A04/A06 instead of A07.

So the picture: Before, there was a loop involving A07: many activities (A01, A03, A04) led to A07, and A07 led to A06/A05, and A05 led back to A01, A06 led to A03/A04. So a cycle: A01 → A07 → A05 → A01 (before: A01→A07 0.94, A07→A05 0.43, A07→A06 0.41, A05→A01 0.96, A06→A03 0.64, A06→A04 0.36, A03→A07 0.51, A04→A07 0.41).

After: A01 → A05 (0.57), A05 → A07 (0.91), A07 → A01 (0.94). So now the cycle is A01 → A05 → A07 → A01. A07's participation dropped from 0.505 to 0.29, and A07 now occurs later in the trace (mean position 0.51 → 0.69). A01's participation doubled (0.275 → 0.53) and A01 is now more often repeated (recurrence 0.11 → 0.29, mean occurrences 0.525 → 1.095).

So the loop was restructured: previously the loop went through A07 early (A01 → A07 directly), now A07 is entered via A05 and occurs later, and the loop passes through A05. A07 is executed less often overall (participation halved from ~50% to ~29% of traces), while A01 is executed more often (participation doubled from ~28% to ~53%).

REL evidence:

REL001 (A01, A03): cooccurrence 0.275 → 0.53; B_only (A03 only) 0.23 → 0. So before, in ~23% of traces A03 occurred without A01; after, they always co-occur when either occurs (A_only 0, B_only 0). Interleaved 0.11 → 0.29.

REL004 (A01, A06): cooccurrence 0.275 → 0.53; B_only (A06 only) 0.23 → 0. Before A06 often occurred without A01; after they co-occur.

REL002 (A01, A04): cooccurrence 0.275 → 0.53; B_only (A04 only) 0.23 → 0.

Hmm, before A05 preceded A01 in ~17% of traces; after never in a fixed order before, but interleaved rose. Wait, A_only 0.24 means A01 occurs without A05 in 24% of traces. LAG001 (A01, A05): lag 1 0 → 0.20; A01 immediately followed by A05 became common. LAG002 (A01, A06): lag 1 0 → 0.41; A01 immediately followed by A06 became common. Hmm interesting — A01 → A06 direct.

LAG014 (A07, A06): before lag 1 0.41; after lag 1 0.63, lag 2 0.375. Support after only 8 — weak.

LAG008 (A04, A07): before lag 1 0.23, lag 2 0.22; after lag 3 0.36, lag 4 0.29, lag 5 0.26. So A04 → A07 became more distant.

LAG005 (A03, A07): before lag 1 0.29; after lag 4 0.38, lag 5 0.27. More distant.

Along with this, A07 is executed less often (participation ~50% → ~29% of traces) and later in the trace, while A01 is executed more often (~28% → ~53%) and more often repeated.

The relational evidence (DIR, LAG, REL) directly shows the successor changes and the direct-succession changes. The pattern is highly consistent across 35 items. The screening count is many times the chance expectation. The competing explanation would be... sampling variability? The screening comparison addresses that at the aggregate level. Another competing explanation: a shift in path frequencies vs a structural change. The condition for "existing paths taken with different frequencies" requires that every activity involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows and only the shares shift. Here, A07's participation dropped from 0.505 to 0.29 — still substantial. But the DIR evidence shows new edges appearing (A01→A05, A07→A01, A05→A07) and old edges disappearing (A01→A07, A07→A05, A05→A01). That's a change in ordering constraints / reordering, not just frequency shares. Actually the swap of A05 and A07 in the loop is a change in ordering constraints.

Here we have before: A01→A07→A05; after: A01→A05→A07.
